newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analyst sees 2.1 mln T British barley for malting.
newsitem.headline: Analyst sees 2.1 mln T British barley for malting.

text.p: British malting barley supply should more than offset domestic demand this year, despite quality fears, French analyst Strategie Grains said on Monday.
In its August report the analyst said some 2.1 million tonnes of barley could qualify for malting while domestic demand could reach 1.95 million tonnes.

"We are assuming that 55 percent and 60 percent of the winter and spring malting barley, respectively, will indeed be fit for malting. There is thus a margin between potential supply and domestic demand: the UK should not need to import malting barley," it said.
Some 660,000 hectares were sown to malting varieties in 1997, including 250,0000 ha of winter barley.

In the report drawn from data available up to August 11, the analyst said 70 percent of the winter barley harvest had been completed. Field reports showed spring barley fared much better than winter barley.

Strategie Grains said it had raised its forecast for spring barley yields to 5.2 tonnes from 5.08 tonnes last month and 5.47 tonnes in 1996. It kept its forecast for winter barley yields unchanged from last month at 6.2 tonnes but down from 6.6 tonnes last year. It expects Britain to produce 7.76 million tonnes of barley in 1997 against 7.78 milllion tonnes in 1996.

It kept its estimate for soft wheat yields unchanged from last month at 7.75 tonnes per hectare against 8.15 tonnes last year. This could result in a soft wheat crop of 15.7 million tonnes against from 16.10 million in 1996.
Substantial rain in June and July and showers in August have raised fears that milling wheat and malting barley quality could be hit but only test results will provide firm indications.
